brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Full hex base at 0,0 plus a north-half base at 1,0, joined and bolted (lockJoints).

One 3-compartment bin sits in the full base and hangs on its rim, so it can be lifted out. A full cover now closes the top of that cell, and the cover has to come off before the bin can be removed. There is only one bin, not several.
A drawer on the cut face of the half base at 1,0.
A handle on top of the full cover, seated on three female-and-male insert stacks. check_build reports no issues and no mesh clashes.
The build is compact, with open faces capped. I did not check weight or strength, and the material is the user's choice.

finish.summary: The build is a full hex base with one 3-compartment bin, a half base carrying a drawer, and a carry handle on the full cover over the bin. Open faces are capped and the joints are bolted. check_build is clear. I did not dress it with props.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
